name: cli-deprecated-command-surface-lifecycle
instr:
Let applications describe obsolete command and flag spellings, guide users toward supported replacements, and inspect deprecated usage after execution. Apply one deprecation policy consistently across invocation, help, suggestions, documentation, runtime completion, and fish completion. Existing applications that declare no deprecations must behave exactly as before.

A command exposes its optional `Deprecation`, while each `DeprecatableFlag` exposes `DeprecatedAliases() []DeprecatedAlias` so aliases can be deprecated independently without affecting canonical or undeclared spellings. `DeprecationPolicy` selects `DeprecationVisible`, `DeprecationHidden`, or `DeprecationReject`; rejection returns `DeprecationError` before the obsolete command's callbacks execute. Replacements are resolved against the active command graph, and only valid non-self replacements are advertised, although unresolved declarations remain diagnostic metadata. Each `Run` produces a fresh `DeprecationReport` containing every actual deprecated spelling in traversal and argv order, and the report survives action or lifecycle errors. Recording repeated aliases must not alter duplicate rejection, boolean counts, or final parsed values. Suggestions prefer supported spellings; visible mode may annotate an otherwise unmatched deprecated suggestion, while hidden mode omits it.
